requirement: All assessments MUST use the SDK graph and source tools. A read uses the node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp`. A delivered read records that node’s fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`. The source project follows {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.authoring.source_tools`. I judged it against its own text only. The three cited requirements (`read_node.mcp`, `read_node.inputs`, `local_provider`) are context, so I did not reassess their own tests.

**1. All assessments use the SDK graph and source tools.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bedrock_cli_uses_selected_profile_region_and_converse_tools]` runs the CLI end to end. It asserts the exact sorted tool set sent to the model: `finish_search`, `get_next_page`, `github`, `list_sources`, `lookup_requirements`, `outgoing_edges`, `outline_source`, `read_node`, `run_named_query`, `search_structure`, `search_text` and `submit_result`.
- It also checks the `read_node` schema fields (`path`, `location`, `node`, `data`).
- It checks that the delivered read result contains the source text.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[explicit_ignored_reads_return_an_error_and_the_assessment_continues]` drives `read_node`, `list_sources`, `search_text` and `search_structure` through the harness.
- `tests/live_bedrock.rs#fn[live_bedrock_authoring]` is the live check that at least one read or search tool is used. It is skipped when `CI` is set.

**2. A read uses the node address.**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_and_example_assessments_record_selected_and_explicit_reads]` reads with `{path, location}` (`fn[second]`) and with `{data:{Definition:...}}`.
- The Bedrock test reads with `{path, location:"line@..."}`.
- The ignored-read test covers a malformed `node` (the "invalid node ID" error) and a missing path.
- Address resolution itself belongs to the cited `read_node.mcp` requirement.

**3. A delivered read records that node's fingerprint.**
- The citation/example test asserts that `inputs` contains the outline input for the read `fn[second]` and for `fn[first]`, which was reached through a search. It also asserts that the explicitly read definition `terms.unused` is recorded with its text.
- It asserts that the unread `fn[untouched]` is not recorded.
- The Bedrock test asserts that the recorded `extra.txt` inputs equal `outline_inputs_for_lines` for the read line.
- The ignored-read test asserts that a failed or excluded read leaves no trace in the evidence (`!evidence.contains("untracked")`).
- The delivery-timing example in `read_node.inputs` belongs to that cited requirement.

**4. The source project follows `local_provider`.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` runs with and without a Git repository. It covers nested `.gitignore` exceptions, untracked files, a tracked-but-ignored file, and an excluded directory.
- It covers `.git` metadata and a `..` scope that escapes the project directory.
- It checks list, read, parse, text search and scoped search. Direct reads of excluded files return an error.
- The ignored-read CLI test covers the agent path. An explicit read of an ignored file returns an error mentioning "excluded" without leaking content, and ignored files do not appear in the list or in text and structural search results. The assessment continues after the error.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_inputs_can_read_untracked_declarations_and_terms]` covers untracked files being available.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/search.rs#mod[tests]/fn[byte_search_reports_case_sensitive_one_based_matching_lines]` is marked as a test but is only tangential.

The assertions enforce the expected outcomes, and each obligation has at least one exercising scenario. I found no unmarked relevant tests and no unresolved ambiguity.

text: :::{req} source_tools

All assessments MUST use the SDK graph and source tools. A read uses the node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.mcp`. A delivered read records that node’s fingerprint under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.inputs`. The source project follows {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`.
:::{req} read_node.mcp
Give `read_node` a node address under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`. The result contains the node’s text. If more
text remains, pass `next` to `get_next_page`.
```text
read_node(NodeAddress) -> {text: string, next?: UUID}
// For a source node the result has these additional fields:
{file: string, selector: string, children: {node: NodeId, file: string, selector: string, header?: string}[]}
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
:::{req} local_provider
Source inspection uses the project directory and respects `.gitignore`,
including nested ignore files and their exceptions. Untracked files are
available unless ignored. The same scope applies to listing, reading,
outlining, text search, and structural search, including requests naming a
file or subdirectory directly.
Files outside the project directory and Git metadata are excluded. A direct
read of an excluded file returns an error.
